article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Cereal A La Mode × Sherb Z
Breeder: Powerzzzup Genetics
THC Content: 22–27%
CBD Content: Generally below 0.1%
Terpene Profile: linalool , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Cinnamon, sweet cream, vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Cinnamon Milk is one of those modern marijuana strains whose name sounds almost too literal until the jar opens. Warm baking spice, creamy sweetness, vanilla, and a faint cereal-like richness come forward first, followed by earthy gas that gives the aroma considerably more weight than a simple dessert cultivar. Powerzzzup Genetics created the hybrid by crossing Cereal A La Mode with Sherb Z, combining two lines already centered on flavor but pushing the offspring toward something unusually specific. The best expressions can genuinely suggest sweetened milk dusted with cinnamon, yet the effect is much stronger than the comforting profile implies. A euphoric mental lift develops early, then gradually gives way to a heavier, stoney body sensation that places the cultivar firmly in the relaxing side of contemporary cannabis.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Cereal A La Mode × Sherb Z. Powerzzzup Genetics created the cross, while Cookies helped introduce and distribute it to a much broader commercial audience. Cereal A La Mode is itself a Powerzzzup creation combining Cereal Milk with Georgia Pie , giving the family tree a strong foundation of cream, vanilla, fruit, dough, and gas. Sherb Z contributes another layer of sweet fruit and dessert aromatics while reinforcing the relaxing physical character that becomes more noticeable later in the high.

Cereal A La Mode is especially important to understanding the flavor. Its own profile centers on condensed milk, graham cracker, creamy vanilla, sugary cereal, berries, and gas. Adding Sherb Z shifts that sweetness toward more floral, candy-like, and resinous territory while preserving enough fuel to keep the finished weed from becoming one-dimensional. The result is not merely another creamy hybrid; the unusual cinnamon-spice note gives it a recognizable identity even among other Cookies-associated dessert strains .

Because the cultivar became commercially visible through Cookies, some references credit Cookies and Powerzzzup jointly as breeders. The more precise description is that Powerzzzup created the genetics and the strain became closely associated with Cookies through collaboration and release.
Effects and Experience

The first stage often feels brighter than the indica-dominant label suggests. A noticeable sense of euphoria can lift mood quickly, making conversation, music, gaming, or casual entertainment more engaging. Some consumers find the early portion surprisingly social and mentally clear, especially at modest doses. That lighter beginning reflects the balanced nature of its dessert-family genetics rather than the abrupt heaviness associated with older Afghan-style weed.

As time passes, the body begins to catch up. Physical tension can soften, the limbs feel heavier, and the initial mental animation settles into a slower, more comfortable rhythm. Cookies describes the effect as a stoney whole-body high, which captures the later stage well. Larger servings can become significantly more sedating and may be better suited to evenings, movies, or simply winding down.

Potency is substantial. Licensed flower has appeared around 22–27% THC, and that level is strong enough to overwhelm inexperienced consumers if the dose is too large. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, short-term memory disruption, appetite stimulation, and anxiety are all possible when THC intake exceeds personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

For some medical marijuana consumers, the combination of mood elevation and later body relaxation may be useful when everyday stress or physical tension makes it difficult to settle down. The earlier cerebral effect can make the experience feel less immediately sedating, while the heavier second half may suit consumers looking for evening relief.

THC-rich cannabis is also used by some patients for appetite loss, nausea, discomfort, and sleep-related problems. Cinnamon Milk may produce those kinds of effects, particularly at larger doses, but that should not be confused with evidence that this specific strain treats any medical condition.

No controlled clinical trial has established Cinnamon Milk as a treatment for insomnia, anxiety, depression, chronic pain, or other disorders. Medical users should rely on laboratory results from the actual product rather than strain reputation alone and should discuss marijuana use with a qualified healthcare professional when prescription medications or serious health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Cinnamon is the feature that separates this cultivar from most cream-heavy weed. The aroma frequently starts with warm spice and sweet dairy-like richness, then expands into vanilla, earth, dough, and light gas. Breaking apart the flower can make the sharper notes more obvious, adding pepper, herbs, and a faint sour edge beneath the sweeter surface.

Current licensed flower provides useful chemical context. One Klutch batch measured 1.58% total terpenes and was led by linalool, limonene, and myrcene. Linalool fits naturally with the softer floral-spice character, limonene adds brightness and faint citrus, while myrcene supports the earthy and musky foundation. Other batches may include greater caryophyllene expression, reinforcing pepper and baking-spice notes.

On the palate, cream and cinnamon often appear together, followed by vanilla and sweet cereal. Earth and gas arrive later, giving the exhale more depth than the aroma initially suggests. Well-cured flowers may also reveal nutty, floral, or mildly fruity accents depending on the harvest.
Growing Information

Reliable breeder-issued cultivation data remain limited because Cinnamon Milk is primarily encountered as commercial flower rather than a broadly documented seed release with an official grow guide. Available cultivation sources commonly place flowering around eight to nine weeks and describe the plant as having moderate stretch rather than either extreme squatness or Haze-like height.

The flowers themselves tend to mature into chunky, dense clusters with dark green and royal-purple coloration, long orange pistils, and heavy trichome coverage. That structure makes airflow especially important during late bloom. Dense cannabis buds can trap moisture, so humidity control becomes increasingly important as the flowers gain mass.

Yield is generally described as medium to high, although no trustworthy breeder-standard gram figure has been published. Outdoor growers would typically expect a late-September-to-October finish if the plant follows the commonly reported eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle. Because provenance matters with newer commercial cultivars, growers seeking authentic material should verify clone or seed origin carefully rather than assuming any plant sold under the Cinnamon Milk name represents the Powerzzzup cut.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Cinnamon Milk?

Cinnamon Milk is Cereal A La Mode × Sherb Z. Powerzzzup Genetics created the strain, and Cookies became closely associated with its commercial release. Cereal A La Mode itself comes from Cereal Milk × Georgia Pie.
Is Cinnamon Milk indica or sativa?
It is generally classified as an indica-dominant hybrid. The effects can feel more balanced at first, with euphoria and mental lift appearing before heavier physical relaxation develops.
How strong is Cinnamon Milk weed?
Commercial flower commonly tests around 22–27% THC. One official Cookies Thailand batch was listed at 26.72% THC with only 0.04% CBD, placing the cultivar firmly in high-potency territory.
What does Cinnamon Milk taste like?

Expect cinnamon, sweet cream, vanilla, baking spice, earth, and gas. Some batches also reveal floral, nutty, citrus, or cereal-like notes. The creamy cinnamon profile is the cultivar’s most distinctive sensory characteristic.
How long does Cinnamon Milk take to flower?

Most cultivation references place flowering around eight to nine weeks. Powerzzzup and Cookies do not currently publish a definitive official flowering schedule, so that range should be treated as a practical cultivation estimate rather than a breeder guarantee.
Final Thoughts on Cinnamon Milk

Cinnamon Milk stands out because its flavor is more specific than the generic “dessert strain” label suggests. Powerzzzup combined the creamy, cereal-like richness of Cereal A La Mode with the sweet fruit and relaxing influence of Sherb Z, then landed on a profile where cinnamon spice, vanilla, earth, and gas remain easy to distinguish from one another.

The effects follow the same layered structure. An approachable euphoric beginning gradually turns heavier and more physical, while high THC gives the experience enough strength for seasoned consumers to take seriously. For cannabis enthusiasts who enjoy Cookies-era genetics but want something beyond fruit candy and sugary gas, Cinnamon Milk offers a warmer, spiced interpretation of modern dessert weed.
